What Is Product-Led Growth?

Explainerlowob research

By lowob · 17 November 2026 · 5-minute read · Growth

Product-led growth (PLG) is a go-to-market motion in which the product does most of the work of acquiring, converting and expanding customers. People sign up, try it free or cheaply and start paying when it proves useful; sales, if there is a sales team, joins later to grow the account. It suits products that deliver value without a conversation and a buyer who can decide alone. Benchmarks suggest only a small share of free users ever pay, so the economics depend on volume and on what happens after sign-up.

What product-led growth means

In a sales-led motion a seller creates the first experience of the product, usually in a demo. In a product-led motion the product creates it, and an in-product prompt or the pricing page asks for payment.

lowob's comparison of the three main motions, Product-Led vs Sales-Led vs Partner-Led Growth, sets the conditions. PLG needs value without a conversation, a short time to value and a price low enough for one person to decide. It breaks when setup, integration or approval is required.

PLG comes in several forms. The terms are used loosely, so the table gives the working definitions used here.

FormWhat the user getsWhat triggers paymentFits whenMain risk
FreemiumA permanently free tier with limitsHitting a usage, feature or team limitLarge market, low cost to serve a free userFree users who never pay but cost money
Free trialFull or near-full product for a fixed periodThe trial endingValue shows inside the trial periodUsers who do not activate before it ends
Product-led salesFree or trial use, then a seller contacts active accountsA sales conversation prompted by usage signalsLarger accounts that need a contract or security reviewSellers chasing usage that is not buying intent

How it works

The motion runs as a funnel, and each step has its own measure. Kyle Poyar's summary of OpenView and Pendo's 2023 benchmark, drawn from more than 1,000 products, gives an illustrative freemium funnel: 1,000 unique visitors a day produce about 90 sign-ups, a 9% conversion. Those produce four or five paying customers, about 5% of sign-ups, over 30 to 60 days, with initial spend of $10 to $100 a month.

The arithmetic explains why PLG suits large markets. At those rates, 1,000 visitors a day yield roughly 120 to 150 new paying customers a month. A niche B2B product with 50 visitors a day does not have the volume to run on self-serve alone.

Activation is the step that decides the rest. OpenView's 2022 report found 87% of standout PLG companies identify and track activation, meaning the moment a new user first gets real value. Seats, Usage or Outcomes defines it as a first real task within a week of signing up, and argues that a free tier is acquisition spend: report it as a channel with a cost per acquired team, and keep free users out of board numbers.

StageMeasureQuestion it answers
Visit to sign-upSign-up rateDoes the offer make sense before trying it?
Sign-up to activationShare activated within a set periodDoes the product show value without help?
Activation to paidFree-to-paid conversionIs the value worth paying for?
Paid to expansionNet revenue retentionDoes use spread through the account?
Free tier costCost per acquired paying teamIs the free tier cheaper than other channels?

Why it matters for a commercial team

Buyer behaviour supports the motion. Gartner's survey of 646 B2B buyers, run in August and September 2025, found 67% prefer a rep-free experience, up from 61% in its 2024 survey. The same research found 45% had used AI during a recent purchase.

The growth figures need care. OpenView's 2022 finding that product-led companies were twice as likely to double revenue came from a survey of founders who chose to respond, and fast-growing firms may adopt PLG rather than PLG causing fast growth.

PLG also meets a limit in larger deals. Once a purchase needs procurement, security review or several approvers, a buying committee takes over and the self-serve path stalls. Most B2B firms that start product-led add a sales team for these accounts.

The product can win the user. A contract above a certain size still needs a person to win the committee.

In lowob's model, sign-up and usage events are part of the store, and the definition of "activated" belongs in the shared definitions so people and agents read it the same way. An agent can flag accounts whose usage crosses a threshold. The decision to contact one, and the reason, is a recorded decision, and nothing sends to the customer without a person.

lowob takeaways

  • The product makes the first sale. Sales joins later, to expand accounts or handle complex purchases.
  • Volume decides viability. With about 5% of free sign-ups paying, small markets struggle to run on self-serve.
  • Activation is the lead measure. Define it in writing and track it before free-to-paid conversion.
  • Plan the hand-off. Record which usage signals trigger a sales contact and whether they predicted a sale.

Sources and notes

  • Forrester, Product-Led Growth: A Forrester Overview, updated 6 August 2025. Analyst summary page; full report behind paywall.
  • OpenView, Third Annual Product Benchmarks Report (press release), 7 June 2022. Investor research; self-selected sample of product-led founders, growth findings are correlation.
  • Kyle Poyar, Growth Unhinged: Your guide to SaaS product metrics, 19 July 2023. Investor commentary on OpenView and Pendo's 2023 benchmark; the funnel is an illustrative average.
  • Gartner, Gartner Sales Survey Finds 67% of B2B Buyers Prefer a Rep-Free Experience, 9 March 2026. Analyst survey of 646 buyers; stated preference, not observed behaviour.
  • Gartner, Gartner Sales Survey Finds 61% of B2B Buyers Prefer a Rep-Free Buying Experience, 25 June 2025. Analyst survey of 632 buyers in 2024; used for the year-on-year comparison.

Next move

Write down, in one sentence, what counts as an activated user for your product, then pull last quarter's sign-ups and count how many met it within a week. If nobody can agree the sentence, that is the first decision to make.
